items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...Earl Hines -- [INTERVIEWEE] That's right, yes, I was.

ctx.x: It's the only time we ever worked together, ever.

Just speaking about festivals of the past, it seems like it's countless now, the number of festivals (inaudible) you've been around. And even starting in the '50s, you were pretty active. You were out here, I think, in one memorable one I recall that had Roy Eldridge, Ben Webster, Earl Hines --

items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: he's the only person I've ever known in my entire life that sounds like Professor

ctx.x: Yes, on his own system of improvisational techniques.
That's quite possible. He's just very complex. I told Frank, I said, 'If it isn't complex, then it isn't your book.' But I just hope it's understandable, so other people can share it.

Well, I accused him -- many years ago, one of our very first clinician sessions and -- and I walked into a class he was working with, and I came out shaking my head and saying, he's the only person I've ever known in my entire life that sounds like Professor -- what's the guy's name?
